newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus voters say yes, yes, yes to Lukashenko.
newsitem.headline: Belarus voters say yes, yes, yes to Lukashenko.

text.p: Belarussian voters backed President Alexander Lukashenko on all seven questions in Sunday's controversial referendum, electoral authorities announced on Monday.

On the most important issue, support for his new draft of the constitution, Lukashenko won the support of 70.5 percent of the 7.2 million registered electorate, electoral commission president Lidiya Yermoshina said. Voter turnout was 84 percent.
An alternative draft constitution proposed by parliament won only 7.9 percent support -- another victory for Lukashenko.
The president has been at odds with parliament over his moves to rewrite the constitution to widen his powers and extend his term of office.
His proposal to switch the national holiday to July 3, the anniversary of the World War Two liberation of Minsk by the Soviet Army, was supported by 88.2 percent.
Abolition of the death penalty won only 17.9 percent and only 15.3 percent supported a free market in land. Lukashenko opposed both ideas.

Two other parliamentary proposals opposed by the president also failed. Only 29.9 percent of voters supported the idea of local officials being elected directly, and 32.1 percent supported the idea of doing away with off-budget funding of government spending.
